a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Direct absolute/relative oral bioavailability measurements for structurally related beta-blockers all exceed the 20% threshold: pamatolol 64.9–103.5%, practolol 90–100%, pindolol 53–79.5%, diacetolol 30–43%, bufuralol 52–83%, and CP-331,684 27%.

L4 absorption evidence shows no solubility or permeability liability for the beta-blocker class: atenolol >1 mg/mL, acebutolol 4.08 mg/mL, propranolol high Caco-2 permeability ~3.4–3.7×10^-5 cm/s, and the closest urea-containing analog has water solubility 1.0 mg/mL.

L5 C78 shows celiprolol, a structurally similar aryloxypropanolamine urea, is subject to intestinal P-gp efflux; itraconazole increases its absorption. This is mechanistic evidence that rifampin (a P-gp inducer) could reduce absorption of the query, but it does not quantify F or establish F<20%.

Other L5 records concern propranolol (high passive permeability, no efflux), atenolol (low permeability/paracellular), and salbutamol (no P-gp effect); they do not provide affirmative threshold-relevant low-F evidence for the query.
L3 exposure reductions for nadolol with EGCG and albuterol with food involve different molecules and co-treatments and do not establish F below 20%.
